subject: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Patel <john.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Hi John —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment moving into the bake-off: 

Pain points you called out:
- High inference cost at peak for the customer support summarization pipeline (current spend ~$18k/mo for cloud endpoints).
- 95th percentile latency spikes during midday traffic causing UI timeouts (users see >1.5s P95 for 512-token prompts).
- Inconsistent extraction quality on short-form inputs (entity F1 varies between 0.630.75).
- Compliance: requirement to retain audit logs + deterministic outputs for certain regulated workflows.

Current stack / constraints:
- Primary: hosted cloud endpoints (managed instances from vendor X) for production; some internal experiments with vLLM running on GCP preemptible GPUs.
- Dataset: ~250k support conversations (we agreed to provide 3 smaller slices for the bake-off).
- Security: needs VPC connectivity and audit-log export; cannot send PII to unknown third-party services without DPA in place.

Success criteria (we discussed):
1) Latency: P95 for 512-token prompts <= 400ms for single-request common paths; target <= 200ms if we can use dedicated capacity + optimized batching.
2) Cost: competitive per-token unit economics vs current cloud endpoints (target ~3030% lower total inference cost at your current traffic profile).
3) Quality: extraction F1 >= 0.82 on the provided eval set, hallucination rate < 5% on the sampling prompts.
4) Operational: VPC-ready deployment option, audit-log export to your S3, and a defined rollback plan.

Bake-off scope we propose:
- Three benchmark buckets: latency (P50/P95/P99) for 64/256/512 token prompts, throughput (tokens/sec) under steady-state and burst, and quality (F1 / hallucination rate) on your eval slices.
- Comparative runs against: your current cloud endpoints, vLLM baseline (your infra), TGI baseline (if you want us to run it), and Redwood Dedicated + Redwood Optimize config.
- We'll provide a test-harness and a benchmark template (attached) — we ask you to sign the simple MOU so we can spin up Dedicated test capacity and share logs.

Next steps / asks for Acme:
- Please send the 3 eval slices (anonymized) and the representative traffic profile by EOD Tuesday (2026-03-10).
- Confirm whether you want Redwood to run the vLLM/TGI baselines on your infra (we can run them if you give temporary access) or if you'll run them and share results.
- Procurement: include procurement@acme.com on the MOU review; I'll send the MOU + SLA doc we referenced.

Attachments: acme-bakeoff-benchmark-template.xlsx (simple runner + metrics to fill), redwood-bakeoff-sla.pdf

I'll schedule the kickoff for the week of 3/16 assuming we get the eval slices this week. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite for a short kickoff and a tech deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acme bake-off: discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures everything we discussed. A few clarifications / requests from our side: 

- Eval slices: we'll redact PII and send three slices (support-short, support-long, billing-extract) by EOD Tuesday.
- Latency targets: 400ms P95 is our minimum; the 200ms target would be ideal. For acceptance we'll accept <= 400ms P95 for the 512 token path, provided the quality bar is met.
- Quality metrics: we use a combination of automated F1 and a small human spot-check (10% sample). Can you include guidance for how you measure hallucination rate in the template?
- Benchmark comparisons: please run Redwood Dedicated vs your hosted API. For vLLM/TGI we will run the tests internally (we plan to run the vLLM setup on our GCP nodes) and share the logs; if Redwood can provide the test harness runner script that would speed things up.
- Security / compliance: procurement will need your DPA + SOC 2 Type II evidence; please send the documents to procurement@acme.com.

Procurement loop: procurement@acme.com, please confirm the best contact for DPA review and timing.

Thanks,
John
Director of ML Ops, Acme Corp
john.patel@acme.com
